1. Outside view. The base rate for this series shows a mean week-over-week change of 1.03 points. From early September to early October 2026, the net rating deteriorated rapidly from -31.6 to -39.3. Since then, it has demonstrated a modest recovery, improving by 2.3 points over five weeks to reach -37.0 on November 6. A naive linear extrapolation of this recent upward trend (+0.46 points per week) over the missing two weeks (Nov 13 and Nov 20) would predict a value around -36.1.

2. Inside view. We are forecasting for November 20, two and a half weeks after the 2026 midterm elections. News reports indicate the Democrats successfully flipped several states, signaling a challenging national environment for President Trump (whose net approval was around -27). Historical patterns show that a settled midterm election—often resulting in divided government—tends to remove immediate political uncertainty, occasionally translating into a slight stabilization or improvement in consumer and voter economic sentiment. This suggests the slow positive momentum seen throughout late October and early November should persist, though likely without sharp spikes since partisan economic views (especially among Republicans who might be discouraged by the midterm losses) will keep a ceiling on any rapid recovery. I estimate this election-settlement factor contributes an additional +0.3 to the naive extrapolation, bringing us to -35.8.

3. Pre-mortem. If this forecast is badly wrong, it is likely because the midterm results triggered a partisan divergence: Republican respondents might suddenly downgrade their view of the economy post-election due to Democratic gains, overpowering the relief from reduced uncertainty and sending the tracker back toward -38.0 or -39.0. Alternatively, a post-election market rally could pull the rating up faster than expected toward -33.0. To correct for this, I will widen my standard deviation to account for a two-week blind spot and potential post-election volatility.

4. Calibrate. With a mean weekly change of 1.03, the expected movement over two weeks is around 1.45 points. Given the potential for post-election shifts in partisan sentiment, I will set an SD of 1.7. This means there is roughly a 68% chance the actual value lands between -37.5 and -34.1, which comfortably covers both a stagnation scenario and an accelerated recovery.
